subject: Cross-region interconnect validation (EU <-> APAC) — acceptance criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@telco-partner.com>, sre-team@acme-robotics.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Cross-region interconnect validation (EU <-> APAC) — acceptance criteria & next steps

Hi all,

Thanks for the initial topology sketches — attached the annotated interconnect we discussed (interconnect-topology-v2.svg) and a proposed IP allowlist for the test window (ip-allowlist-proposal.csv).

Goal: run a controlled warm-standby connectivity validation between our EU sovereign VPC (Frankfurt) and the APAC on-prem cluster (Singapore) before we sign the residency attestation. We need a short, auditable test that covers: BGP adjacency, prefix advertisement, KV-cache replication window (small sample), end-to-end latency/MTU, and a failover cutover exercise (non-production).

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- BGP established with prefix visibility on both sides (no more than 2 next-hop hops).
- MTU stable at 9000 end-to-end (or documented degradation and workaround).
- Prefix propagation delay under 10s for announced prefixes in both directions.
- Controlled failover: redirect 10% of test requests to APAC variant and confirm response consistency for a selected prompt set.
- Signed interconnect acceptance note from Acme SRE and Redwood network team.

Can I get: (1) preferred 2-hour test window next week (UTC ranges), (2) contact for on-site console during test, and (3) any divergences we should add to the acceptance criteria?

Thanks — looping in Lauren & Karthik to own Redwood network checklist.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: interconnect-topology-v2.svg (image), ip-allowlist-proposal.csv (csv)
From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@telco-partner.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: sre-team@acme-robotics.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 09:45:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Cross-region interconnect validation (EU <-> APAC) — acceptance criteria & next steps

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provision the cross-connect and establish BGP on our side; proposed test windows (UTC): May 21 02:00–04:00 or May 22 00:00–02:00. Raj (ACME SRE) will be on the bridge.

Notes from our infra: we see potential MTU pathology over the public peering if middleboxes enforce 1500 — we can support jumbo frames if the transit leg is configured accordingly. Suggest adding an MTU fallback acceptance item (measured degradation + packet capture).

I’ve also attached our initial community tagging table and suggest we agree on 2 reserved communities for traffic steering during the failover (bgp-community-table.csv).

—Rajiv
Rajiv Shah
Network Products — Telco Partner
Attachments: bgp-community-table.csv (csv)

Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cross-region interconnect validation (EU <-> APAC) — acceptance criteria & next steps

Team —

I like the draft acceptance criteria. A few operational asks before we lock the window:

- Inventory: confirm the ASN, BGP neighbors, and full prefix list for both sides (we will need to keep a signed snapshot).
- Observability: ensure we have packet capture on both edges for the MTU test and a set of synthetic prompts (prompt-set-v1) to validate model output parity during the traffic shift.
- Fallback policy: document exact rollback steps if the failover introduces a correctness regression (we should automatically revert traffic split and mark as incident).
- Compliance: Acme must provide a short written attestation that no customer PII will cross the transit during the test (sample statement acceptable).

Adding one acceptance criterion: a documented replay of 200 sample inference requests with matching top-1 responses (allowing nondeterministic differences noted) across EU vs APAC.

Attaching an SLA/difference template (SLA-diff.docx) we can use for sign-off.

Thanks — please confirm the two-hour window you prefer and I’ll schedule the incident bridge.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA-diff.docx (docx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Shah <rajiv@telco-partner.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cross-region interconnect validation (EU <-> APAC) — technical checklist

Laur & Dylan —

Below is the technical checklist Karthik / Redwood network will validate during the window. Please consider these required for acceptance. I’ll be on the bridge and will post live notes to the Jira ticket (NETOPS-421).

Technical checklist (pre-test):
1) Confirm ASNs and peering auth (BGP passwords / MD5).
2) Agree on community map and install on both sides (see bgp-community-table.csv).
3) IP allowlist applied at edge and validated from both control planes.
4) MTU negotiation: run ping-based mtu discovery to confirm path MTU and capture pcap for any fragmentation.
5) KV-cache replication: push a small deterministic write-set to EU primary, read from APAC via warmed cache to confirm TTL/consistency for 60s window.
6) Traceroute and path analysis from three vantage points (Frankfurt, Singapore, and a neutral probe).
7) Traffic shift: 10% split with health checks; automatic rollback policy if error rate >1% or response mismatch >5% during 5m observation window.

Post-test deliverables:
- Signed acceptance note (Acme SRE + Redwood NetOps)
- Packet captures from both edges attached to NETOPS-421
- Short incident report if any deviation from acceptance criteria

Quoting Rajiv: 
> we can provision the cross-connect and establish BGP on our side; proposed test windows (UTC): May 21 02:00–04:00 or May 22 00:00–02:00.

Preference: May 22 00:00–02:00 UTC (less traffic in EU). If that works for Acme, we will lock it and I will schedule the bridge.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@telco-partner.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 16:42:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Cross-region interconnect validation (EU <-> APAC) — test results and acceptance

Dylan / team —

We ran the May 22 window as scheduled (sorry for the delayed note — consolidating sign-offs). Summary: BGP adjacency stable, prefixes visible both ways within 6s, MTU path discovered 9000 end-to-end after updating transit config, and KV-cache read test passed for the 60s sample window. Traffic-shift exercise (10% for 5m) showed no material correctness regressions on our sampled prompt set (attached basic logs).

Deliverables attached: signed interconnect acceptance (signed-acceptance-acme.pdf), packet capture snippets, and the community tagging confirmation. Acme SRE (Raj) also provided the compliance attestation text for the test (PII handling statement) and they will deliver a formal letter to legal.

Next steps: Redwood to ingest the acceptance note into the residency binder and close NETOPS-421. If you want a follow-up rehearsal for a full-scale cutover, we can plan Q3.

—Rajiv
Rajiv Shah
Network Products — Telco Partner
Attachments: signed-acceptance-acme.pdf (pdf), pcap-snippets.zip (zip)
